- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often overpredicts downward moves; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.0 price point to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–3 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5 price points per day post-spike.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or oscillating), model tends to overfit recent trends; apply a 1–2 day smoothing filter or reduce forecast volatility by 10–20%.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates late-period rallies (especially after sentiment turns positive); add 0.5–1.0 price point buffer in final 5–7 days if sentiment > 0.67.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.33 → -0.67 → +0.67), model often misjudges turning points; apply a 2–3 day buffer before reversal to avoid premature sell-off.
